newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo/IMF officials to meet in Washington.
newsitem.headline: Yugo/IMF officials to meet in Washington.

text.p: Yugoslavia's finance minister will hold official talks with the IMF in Washington on Wednesday on restoring its membership with the organisation, an independent Belgrade TV station reported on Tuesday.
The federal Minister of Finance Tomica Raicevic arrived in Washington on Tuesday evening, BK televison said.

"He (Raicevic) will be having a high-level meeting with senior officials from the IMF on Wednesday morning in Washington," said John Eisenhammer of Lowe Bell, who are in charge of Yugoslavia's public relations.
"This is an important visit," he said in a telephone interview. "This is the first visit of a senior government official in an official capacity since sanctions were imposed.
Eisenhammer said the visit shows that progress in Yugoslav/IMF talks was being made.
Raicevic will give the IMF the legal documentation to show that Yugoslavia, now consisting of Serbia and Montenegro, has complied with all the requirements of the fund regarding its membership.
Last week the Yugoslav parliament endorsed what the government described as all conditions set by the IMF to restore Belgrade's membership.
According to Eisenhammer, Raicevic will also pass on to the IMF officials the country's "hope for a favourable response from the board of the IMF to the membership matter".
IMF membership is a crucial step in Belgrade's efforts to bring in foreign capital to repair its economy, crippled by international sanctions imposed because of its role in the war in Bosnia.
Belgrade is also in the throes of negotiating a deal with commercial creditors to settle about $2 billion in debts inherited from the former Yugoslavia.
Bankers say a mountain of issues still have to be resolved, including how to share out the assets left behind after the old Yugoslavia's bloody collapse five years ago.
Even with membership of the IMF, Yugoslavia will still have to make some painful reforms before it is likely to get any financial help from the IMF.
